summary: Before April 1, 2017 PST was not charged to the owner on real property construction contracts; the contractor paid PST on materials as the consumer and recovered it in the contract price.

citations.title: Information Notice IN 2017-02, PST - Services to Real Property (issued March 22, 2017)
citations.quote: Prior to April 1, 2017, labour charges relating to the construction, alteration, repair, erection, remodeling or improvement of real property were not subject to tax.

citations.title: Information Notice IN 2017-02, PST - Services to Real Property (issued March 22, 2017)
citations.quote: the contractor was considered the consumer of materials incorporated into the property and was required to pay PST on the cost of equipment, materials and supplies used or consumed.

notes: Citations of finance.gov.sk.ca bulletins, no longer online there, are archived from Internet Archive captures. 'Exempt' describes the owner's invoice: no separate PST, but embedded PST on materials was recovered in the price ('Provincial Sales Tax Included'). Transition: written contracts entered into before April 1, 2017 (other than master service agreements) stayed under these rules, including change orders of 10% or less of the original contract; so this treatment can apply to invoices after 2017-03-31 for such contracts.

summary: From April 1, 2017 contractors collect Saskatchewan PST on the total charge (labour, materials and related fees) for construction, repair or improvement of real property.

citations.title: Information Notice IN 2017-02, PST - Services to Real Property (issued March 22, 2017)
citations.quote: Effective April 1, 2017, these charges, which were previously exempt from PST, become taxable and PST must be shown as a separate line item on the invoice to the customer.

citations.title: Information Bulletin PST-12, Services to Real Property (revised July 2024)
citations.quote: A contractor engaged in services to real property is required to collect PST on the total charge to the customer for the services, including all related charges and fees such as charges for labour, materials, transportation, insurance, permits, service fees, and any tax, levy or duty, other than the GST.

citations.title: Budget 2017-18 Revenue / Tax Backgrounder (saskatchewan.ca)
citations.quote: New contracts entered into on or after April 1, 2017 will be subject to PST on the total contract price to the purchaser.

notes: Applies to contracts entered into on or after April 1, 2017 (see the transition note on the previous rule). Later narrow exemptions are not in this rule: installation labour for exempt farm equipment (from April 1, 2020), on-farm trenching and dugouts (from April 1, 2022), and installation of special equipment for persons with disabilities (from April 1, 2023), per PST-12. Snow clearing, lawn care and similar maintenance services are not taxable. New homes built for resale are taxed on the builder's selling price excluding land; that is not a contract to an owner.

summary: General management and business consulting is not taxable in Saskatchewan unless it is part of a sale of taxable goods or services.

conditions.when: consulting included in the sale of taxable goods or services (e.g. IT consulting, legal consulting)

citations.title: Information Bulletin PST-46, Service Enterprises (revised February 2025)
citations.quote: General consulting and advisory services are not subject to tax provided they are not included in the sale of taxable goods and services.

notes: The 2009 PST-46 (archived January 2013) has the same list of taxable services, which does not include consulting.

summary: Interior design and decorating services are not on Saskatchewan's list of taxable services, so they are not taxable; goods the designer sells are.

citations.title: Information Bulletin PST-46, Service Enterprises (revised February 2025)
citations.quote: Services that are not within this list of taxable services are non-taxable.

notes: Rests on the list's not naming interior design (checked against PST-46 2025 and 2009); no statement names interior design directly. Installing goods may be a taxable repair or installation service (PST-57) or a service to real property (PST-12).

summary: Engineering and architectural services are taxable when site-specific to land or property in Saskatchewan; other engineering and architectural work is not.

the services are not site-specific to Saskatchewan (e.g. for a project outside the province, or not tied to a site)
the services are in the nature of feasibility studies, environmental studies, or general consulting or advisory services, wherever the project is

citations.title: Information Bulletin PST-65, Engineering, Geoscience and Architecture Services (revised September 2020)

notes: Turns on where the project is, which the code doesn't carry. PST-65's detailed tests were not re-read for the years before 2020.

summary: Charges for the right to use or access prewritten software, including hosted or web-based software, are subject to Saskatchewan PST.

citations.quote: Charges for the use or right-to-use or access web-based, or hosted software are taxable, including when possession of the software is maintained by the software provider or a third-party service provider.

citations.title: Information Bulletin PST-7 (revised March 2012)
citations.quote: Tax must be collected on all charges for new and used computer software, including charges for the right to use software, licence fees, royalty fees

citations.title: Information Bulletin PST-7 (revised March 2012)
citations.quote: (j) The right to use a computer server or other data storage or transmission services.

notes: Citations of finance.gov.sk.ca bulletins, no longer online there, are archived from Internet Archive captures. The explicit 'Software as a Service' paragraph appears only in the later bulletin; for 2013 onward the rule rests on the March 2012 bulletin taxing 'charges for the right to use software' and server use, which is an interpretation that remote access was covered. Non-resident providers' collection obligations were expanded later (IN 2020-08), which concerns registration, not treatment. Other ordinary adult clothing and footwear

summary: Saskatchewan liquor is exempt from PST; the separate 10% Liquor Consumption Tax applies instead and is not included.

citations.title: Saskatchewan PST-33, Restaurants, Caterers and Other Businesses Selling Prepared Food and Beverages (May 2021)
citations.quote: Alcoholic beverages are not subject to PST but are subject to Liquor Consumption Tax (LCT) at a rate of 10 per cent on the total price paid by your customer, excluding GST.

citations.title: Saskatchewan, Liquor Consumption Tax
citations.quote: Liquor Consumption Tax (LCT) is a 10 per cent tax on the total selling price of beer, wine and spirits.

notes: May 2021 revision; first day of month used. LCT applies to retail and licensed-premises sales. GST remains payable; exemption is only from PST.
